claim: Let \(T\subset\mathbb R^3\) be a regular tetrahedron with vertices \(v_0=0,v_1,v_2,v_3\), edge lattice \(L=\sum_{j=1}^3\mathbb Z v_j\), and reciprocal edge lattice \(L^*=\{\xi:\langle\xi,v_j\rangle\in\mathbb Z\text{ for }j=1,2,3\}\). For \(\xi\in L^*\), put \(\lambda_0=0\) and \(\lambda_j=\langle\xi,v_j\rangle\). The Fourier transform of Euclidean surface measure on \(\partial T\) vanishes exactly when the multiset \(\{\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3\}\) has multiplicity type \(1+1+1+1\), type \(2+2\), or type \(2+1+1\) with repeated value \(r\) and singleton values \(s,t\) satisfying \(s+t=2r\).

correctness.rationale: For integer \(p,q\) with \(q\ne0\), direct integration gives \(F_2(p,q)=(\mathbf 1_{\{p=0\}}-\mathbf 1_{\{p=q\}})/(2\pi i q)\); the \(q=0\) cases follow by symmetry and area. Thus each face integral is \(0\) for three distinct integer nodes, \(1/2\) for three equal nodes, and \(-i/(2\pi(s-r))\) for a repeated pair \(r,r\) with singleton \(s\). Each facet contributes the same positive factor \(2A_f\) because \(T\) is regular. Summing the four face terms exhausts partitions \(1+1+1+1\), \(2+2\), \(2+1+1\), \(3+1\), and \(4\). The first two vanish; type \(2+1+1\) vanishes iff \(s+t=2r\); type \(3+1\) has nonzero real part \(1/2\) and type \(4\) has value \(2\) after removing the common factor. The rational finite checker is supplementary, not the proof.

value.rationale: The Fourier zero set of a uniform tetrahedral shell is a natural diffraction and reciprocal-lattice sampling invariant distinct from the volume form factor. The result gives a complete exact classification over all reciprocal-edge-lattice frequencies, including the nontrivial midpoint condition for the \(2+1+1\) multiplicity pattern. It supplies a reproducible structural rule, not just a finite census or normalization check.
